title: Estimate System Solutions from Graphs
student_objective: I can estimate the solution of a real-world system from a graph and interpret the intersection in context.

concept_cards.title: Estimate from the grid
concept_cards.content: When the lines cross between grid marks, read the x- and y-coordinates as reasonable estimates rather than exact integers.

concept_cards.title: Use the axis scale
concept_cards.content: Check what each grid interval represents before reading coordinates. One square may represent 1, 5, 10, or another unit.

concept_cards.title: Interpret both coordinates
concept_cards.content: In context, the x-coordinate and y-coordinate usually represent different quantities. State both with units.

concept_cards.title: Reasonable precision
concept_cards.content: Estimate only as precisely as the graph allows. Do not report more decimal places than the visual supports.

context.teacher_signal: Student gives coordinates without units or meaning.

items.prompt: A graph intersection is halfway between x=4 and x=5. Estimate the x-coordinate.
items.tutor_behavior: Connect visual midpoint to decimal estimate.

solution_steps.explanation: Use an approximation because the value comes from a graph.

items.prompt: If each grid square on the y-axis represents 10 units, what value is 3 squares above 0?
items.tutor_behavior: Read the axis scale before interpreting a point.

solution_steps.explanation: Multiply the number of grid intervals by the scale.

items.prompt: Two cost graphs intersect near (6,42). Interpret this if x is months and y is dollars.
items.answer_key: at about 6 months both costs are about $42
accepted_answers: at about 6 months both costs are about $42
hint_steps: At about 6 months, the two costs are both about $42.

solution_steps.explanation: Both plans have about the same cost there.

items.prompt: A graph uses 2 units per x-grid square. The intersection is 4.5 squares to the right of 0. Estimate x.

solution_steps.explanation: Convert grid-square distance to coordinate value.

items.prompt: The intersection appears at about (3.5,18). If x is hours and y is miles, interpret the point.
items.answer_key: after about 3.5 hours both quantities are about 18 miles
accepted_answers: after about 3.5 hours both quantities are about 18 miles
items.tutor_behavior: Read and interpret both coordinates with units.
hint_steps: At about 3.5 hours, both graphs show about 18 miles.

items.prompt: The x-axis scale is 5 units per square. An intersection lies 7 squares right of 0. Estimate x.
An intersection is slightly above y=12 and below y=13, about one-quarter of the way from 12 to 13. Estimate y.
items.tutor_behavior: Estimate fractional positions between tick marks.
hint_steps: The interval from 12 to 13 is 1 unit.

items.prompt: A graph intersection is approximately (8,55). If x is tickets and y is dollars, interpret it.
items.answer_key: at about 8 tickets both totals are about $55
accepted_answers: at about 8 tickets both totals are about $55
hint_steps: The two totals are about equal at 8 tickets and $55.

items.prompt: The y-axis scale is 20 units per square. The intersection is 2.5 squares above 0. Estimate y.

solution_steps.explanation: Convert the visual distance using the axis scale.

items.prompt: The crossing point is about three-fourths of the way from x=2 to x=3. Estimate x.
A graph intersection is about (5.2,31). If x is days and y is units sold, interpret it.
items.answer_key: after about 5.2 days both models show about 31 units sold
accepted_answers: after about 5.2 days both models show about 31 units sold
hint_steps: The intersection means both models agree at about 5.2 days and 31 units.

items.prompt: If each x-grid interval equals 4 units and the point is 6 intervals from 0, estimate x.
An intersection lies halfway between y=70 and y=80. Estimate y.
Why should you check the axis scale before estimating a graph intersection?
items.answer_key: because each grid interval may represent more than one unit
accepted_answers: because each grid interval may represent more than one unit
the scale changes the coordinate values
hint_steps: A grid square is only a visual interval.
Its numeric value comes from the labels.
You must use the axis scale to convert visual distance to coordinate value.

solution_steps.explanation: The labels determine the numeric value of each interval.

items.prompt: If a graph supports only nearest-tenth estimates, which is more appropriate: 4.7 or 4.736281?
hint_steps: Use only the precision visible on the graph.
